solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bar set back by another's growth?

indicators.note: to set something back is to move it backwards, so its letters are read from the far end

parts.note: a bar is a pub, a place serving drinks
another kind of bar: a crowbar is a lever

explanation.surface: One drinking establishment is overshadowed by a rival's expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is used twice: first as a drinking place, then 'another' bar of a different sort, the metal kind you prise with. The question mark flags that 'growth' is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bupleurum, or hare's ear, is a plant, and anything that grows from the ground can be called a growth.

clue.text: Will's to fit gold optimal frames

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: optimal means the best possible
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone named Will is trying to squeeze gold into the best spectacle frames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is Shakespeare, so 'Will's to fit' asks for his word meaning to fit or suit; the word appears in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used this verb meaning to suit or befit, a sense now obsolete outside his plays.

clue.text: Detective from radical school casing Republican

parts.note: pink is slang for left-leaning or radical

indicators.note: a casing is an outer shell, so one word encloses the letter

parts.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A detective emerging from a revolutionary school that is sheltering a right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the English public school, a common crossword source; here it opens up after its first letter to take R.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Pinkerton founded the famous American private investigation agency, and his name became slang for any private eye.

clue.text: With wife at heart, finally gave back football legend's lost money

indicators.note: finally points at the end of each word, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letters of the two words

indicators.note: something at the heart of another sits inside it, so the letter goes within

parts.note: Pelé, the Brazilian footballer
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A famous footballer, with his wife beside him, at last repays money he lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The W goes inside the footballer's name, after its first letter. 'Lost money' means a currency no longer in use, not money someone mislaid.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency of Equatorial Guinea until replaced by the CFA franc in 1985, so it is a defunct monetary unit.

clue.text: Rating income capacity initially cuts fine owed to victim's family

indicators.note: to cut into something is to enter it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: erk is RAF slang for the lowest rating, an aircraftman

indicators.note: initially points at the start of each word, so only opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A tax assessment of someone's earning power, used to set compensation owed to a victim's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like an assessment, but it is a low-ranked serviceman; erk is British forces slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Irish law this was the blood money paid by a killer to the kin of the person slain.

clue.text: Using diamond, shaped groove in underlying surface

indicators.note: one thing lying in another is held inside it

parts.note: a bed is a layer that something rests upon
a rut is a worn groove

explanation.surface: A craftsman cuts a groove into a base layer with a diamond-tipped tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening three words; the comma makes 'shaped' look like it belongs with the groove.
explanation.definitionFit: Gem cutters brute a diamond by rubbing it against another diamond to rough out its girdle.

clue.text: Port of Spain, primarily capital of Trinidad and Tobago, set in stone

indicators.note: a gem set in a ring is mounted within it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: rock is stone

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

indicators.note: a capital is an upper-case letter, and a name's capital is its first one

parts.note: its opening upper-case letter

explanation.surface: A gazetteer note on the Caribbean: Port of Spain is the capital of Trinidad and Tobago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port of Spain' reads as one name, but 'Port' alone is the definition. 'Capital' means a capital letter, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostock is a German harbour city on the Baltic coast, so it is a seaport.

clue.text: Star team off and on given top-grade mark for pronunciation

indicators.note: switching off and on alternately keeps every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
A is the top grade in exams

explanation.surface: A star team plays well and badly by turns but is still given top marks for diction.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even-placed letters of the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A trema is a diaeresis, the two dots placed over a vowel to show it is sounded separately.

clue.text: What might cause Lydia's ex to suggest daily sex?

definitions.text: What might cause Lydia's ex to suggest daily sex?

indicators.note: a condition that causes misreading jumbles the letters, so they come out in another order

parts.note: the letters of these words, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A woman's former partner seems to be proposing intimacy every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'Lydia's ex' and 'daily sex' use the same eight letters, so a reader who scrambles letters could mistake one for the other; the answer is a third arrangement of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslexia is a reading difficulty in which letters can appear transposed, which would turn one phrase into the other.

clue.text: Poetic inspiration once more delaying international university course

indicators.note: delaying means the I of the word arrives later, after the rest

parts.note: once more means again
PPE, philosophy, politics and economics, is a university degree course

explanation.surface: A student again puts off an international degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying' acts on one letter only: the I for international is held back until after the rest of the once-more word, then the degree course follows. Aganippe is an obscure classical name, so the wordplay carries the solve.
explanation.definitionFit: Aganippe was a spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses, so a source of poetic inspiration in Greek myth.

clue.text: Pens glossy rubbish about visual collection that excludes John

indicators.note: about means around, so one set of letters goes round the other
rubbish is a verb here, to trash, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words
optic means relating to sight

explanation.surface: A critic writes off a glossy photo book that leaves someone called John out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like the verb for writing, and 'John' like a person, but John is the fourth evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew, Mark and Luke share a common view of Jesus's life; John's Gospel stands apart from that trio.

clue.text: Pole agreed to stop destruction after losing face

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so these letters fill a gap inside
the face is the front, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a wreck is destruction
yep is a casual yes

explanation.surface: A Polish person agrees to halt a campaign of destruction once humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a wooden stake. 'Losing face' sounds like disgrace, but just drops the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ryepeck is a stake driven into a riverbed to moor a punt while fishing, so it is a kind of pole.

clue.text: Salt, take note, destroyed satellite boards

indicators.note: to board a vessel is to get inside it, so these letters go in

parts.note: NB is nota bene, Latin for note well
Io is a moon of Jupiter
ate, as in ate away or consumed

explanation.surface: A warning that salt corroded a spacecraft's panels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seawater damage to the satellite but is a chemical salt. Io, a moon of Jupiter, is the usual crossword satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: A niobate is a chemical salt derived from niobic acid, containing the metal niobium.

clue.text: Heading off two ways to outdo Scottish crawler?

indicators.note: with its head taken off, the first word loses its opening letter

parts.note: the first way: to better someone is to surpass them
the second way: to cap a story is to top it

explanation.surface: Advice on two methods of beating a fawning Scottish sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' looks like a toady but is a creepy-crawly. The two verbs meaning to outdo are run together, the first one beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettercap is a Scots word for a spider, a many-legged creature that creeps along.

clue.text: Bridge in Swiss Cottage blocked by gutted overturned vehicle

indicators.note: blocked means obstructed by something lodged inside

parts.note: a chalet is the typical Swiss wooden house

indicators.note: turned over, so read from the other end
gutting removes the insides, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A bridge in the London district of Swiss Cottage is blocked by a wrecked, upturned car.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a London district, which makes 'Bridge in Swiss Cottage' read as a street scene; 'in' is only a link, and the cottage is Swiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalet is the term for the bridge of a stringed instrument, the piece that holds the strings off the body.

clue.text: Reportedly spiteful unit from SE Asia

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

parts.note: catty means spiteful

explanation.surface: A rumour about a malicious army squad from Southeast Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' suggests a military group but is a unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The katti, or catty, is a traditional weight of about 600 grams used across Malaysia, China and neighbouring regions.

clue.text: Incense burners one day placed on unopened scripture books

indicators.note: not opened means the start is missing, so the first letter goes

parts.note: short for Thursday
Bibles are books of scripture

explanation.surface: Censers are set down on closed holy books for a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the day comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurible is the metal censer swung on chains in church services to spread smoke from burning resin.

clue.text: Illegitimate kids bog down unknown US parent from the south

indicators.note: in a vertical entry, reading from the bottom upward runs the letters backwards

parts.note: to mire is to bog down
z is a mathematical unknown
the American spelling of mum

explanation.surface: Children born outside marriage weigh down a mysterious American mother from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the south' looks like the southern US states but means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Hebrew and Yiddish plural of mamzer, a child born of a forbidden union, so bastards.

clue.text: Birds like a pasty's filling

indicators.note: a pasty's filling is what lies inside the crust, so all but the first and last letters

parts.note: a pasty is the classic Cornish dish, so Cornish describes it

explanation.surface: Birds resemble a pie's filling, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cornish pasty is a meat and vegetable pie from Cornwall in south-west England; take the inside of CORNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornis is a rare word for the bird life of a region, its avifauna, so birds collectively.

clue.text: Wriggling insignificant sort mostly turned out miserly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a squirt is an insignificant little person

indicators.note: what is turned out is evicted, so the inside letters are thrown out

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A wriggling nobody proved, for the most part, to be stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' reads as 'proved to be', but it means the middle of the following word is ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirmy describes something that squirms, twisting about restlessly like a worm.

clue.text: Illustration of river, place shrouded in silence

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: something shrouded is wrapped up inside a covering

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means silence
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: A picture of a river and a spot wrapped in quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplum is an example or moral anecdote used to illustrate a point in a sermon or argument.

clue.text: Scarlet dye formerly found in Pyrenean city

indicators.note: what is found in a place is located inside it

parts.note: Pau is a city at the foot of the French Pyrenees
once means formerly

explanation.surface: A red dye that used to be produced in a mountain city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' looks like a comment on the dye's history but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponceau names a family of bright red azo colourants, and also the poppy-red colour itself.

clue.text: Landscape gardener the other side of Hyde?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Gertrude, the famous English garden designer
second meaning: the respectable doctor in Stevenson's tale whose dark self is Mr Hyde

explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is in London, so 'the other side of Hyde' looks like a location for a gardener's work; it is the other half of a split personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Jekyll designed hundreds of gardens, and Dr Jekyll is the good persona whose alter ego is Hyde in Stevenson's novella.

clue.text: Cross president heading for Zaire about endless government rifts

indicators.note: a rift splits something open, so these letters wedge inside
the heading is the top, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: without an end, the final letter is lost

parts.note: rule means government

explanation.surface: An angry president, at the head of Zaire, over splits in a failing administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an angry adjective for the president but is the noun for a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebrula is the hybrid offspring of a male zebra and a female horse, so it is a crossbreed.

clue.text: Court whitewash starts to become apparent before one side turned up

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of the two words

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upwards means read bottom to top

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A legal cover-up starts to come to light before one party reverses its position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court whitewash' reads as a judicial cover-up but is a tennis term. In cricket, leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis slang, a set won six games to love is named after the ring-shaped roll, its zero shape.

clue.text: Caught somebody crushing iodine into poisonous alkaloid

indicators.note: to crush something is to squeeze it tightly, so one word grips the others

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
one, as in someone
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
in, a synonym of into

explanation.surface: Someone is caught grinding iodine into a deadly poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word but contributes two letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Coniine is the toxic alkaloid in hemlock, the poison that killed Socrates.

clue.text: Check fine old tropical fruit on vine

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
OK means fine
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Inspecting an overripe tropical fruit still hanging on its creeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check fine' reads like an instruction about a penalty; both are abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The choko, or chayote, is a pear-shaped gourd grown on a climbing plant in warm countries.

clue.text: Dance record arranged with eg excessively engaging energy

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: to engage is to take in, so one word holds the letter

parts.note: overly means to excess
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dance track is remixed with far too much high-energy content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance record' reads as one thing, a club track, but 'Dance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Roger de Coverley is an old English country dance, often performed at the end of a ball.

clue.text: Anything but horny creatures back from orgy wearing slippers

indicators.note: what is worn is surrounded by the garment, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: mules are backless slippers

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Partygoers at an orgy, wearing only slippers, are anything but aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' tempts the slang sense, but it means having horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Muley cattle are naturally hornless, so they are animals lacking horns entirely.

clue.text: Indian provincial flexible over hosting majority of sport

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one word holds another
turned over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: lissom means supple

indicators.note: the majority is most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sport, as in good fun

explanation.surface: A supple athlete from an Indian province takes on most of the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' as a noun for amusement, as in 'in sport', gives the letters to be shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian usage the mofussil was the rural hinterland away from the main cities, so a provincial area.
